title: He built an ark… but was his heart really clean?
paragraphs: He built an ark… but was his heart really clean?
That’s the tension.
Because when we hear “righteous,” we imagine flawless. Untouched. Pure from start to finish.
But the Bible doesn’t paint fairy tales.
In Genesis 6:9, it says Noah was “a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God.”
Read that slowly.

Not perfect.
Not sinless.
But walking with God.
And here’s what we miss…

Righteousness in Scripture is not about never falling—
it’s about where you stand when God calls.
Some scholars interpret Noah’s righteousness as relational, not absolute—meaning he stood out in a corrupt generation because he trusted and obeyed God when no one else would.

Everyone else was running wild.
Violence. Corruption. Darkness unchecked.
And Noah?
He listened.
He obeyed.
He built… when it made no sense.
That’s not just moral behavior—that’s faith.
Hebrews 11:7 says Noah became “heir of the righteousness that is in keeping with faith.”
There it is.
Faith.

Not self-made goodness.
Not earned approval.
But a man who believed God enough to move.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because after the flood, Noah still stumbled (Genesis 9—he gets drunk).
So no—he wasn’t spotless.
He was chosen.
But not randomly.
He was chosen through faith.
And that points us straight to Jesus.
Because the same pattern holds:

We are not saved because we are flawless.
We are made righteous because we trust the One who is.
Jesus Christ doesn’t look for perfect people—He covers broken ones with His righteousness.

Noah built an ark to survive judgment.
Jesus became the ark to save us from it.
So was Noah righteous—or just chosen?
Both.

Chosen by grace.
Declared righteous through faith.
And that same invitation is still open.

Not “be perfect.”
But “walk with Me.”

Choose faith over pride.
Choose surrender over control.
